messages:
lex: Quick request for launch collateral: marketing needs a validated benchmark pack we can cite (not just a spreadsheet dump). Goal: reproducible claims + an FAQ on edge cases.

lex: Concrete asks: a canonical manifest.csv with provenance + these extra columns: persona, workload_tier (low/medium/high), concurrency, gpu_mem_mb, pathology_flag, payload_sha256. Also need GPU util traces and a p50/p95/p99/p999 breakdown.

chris: Sounds good. For persona, do you want synthetic "chatbot" vs "completion" vs "assistant" labels? Also, how many concurrency levels?

lex: Yes — those three personas. Concurrency levels: 1, 8, 32. For each (persona, seq_len_bucket, concurrency) run 250 requests for steady-state and capture first-120 for coldstart.

maria: We'll run on dedicated-3 pool with the following model tags pinned: redwood/open-llama-7b-v2@20260201, and redwood/cerberus-13b@20260115 for comparison. Variants: fp16, 8bit-q, 4bit-q. We'll also collect GPU mem and GPU util every second.

sam: Uploading initial manifest draft to s3. Example row I added: 
```csv
file,prompt_type,persona,seq_len_bucket,seed,quant,warmup_policy,model_tag,concurrency,expected_percentile_ms,notes,payload_sha256,pathology_flag
short_chat_003.json,chat,assistant,short,101,fp16,steady-5,redwood/open-llama-7b-v2@20260201,1,<=60,conversational turn,sha256:aa11,false
```
Link: s3://redwood-marketing/launch/benchpacks/manifest-draft-v2.csv

jia: We also need a tiny human-readable snippet pack (3 samples per persona/seq bucket) for copy-paste into the blog. Keep them non-sensitive.

anya: Can we add a column 'cpu_spill_count' so marketing knows when requests hit CPU fallback? That'd help us avoid overstating latency for certain payloads.

chris: Good call. Add cpu_spill_count and nvlink_cross_node flag. Also, mark any sample that triggers multimodal preprocessing or large p-kv chains in pathology_flag.

maria: Planning note: warmup_policy names = steady-5 (5 warmups per worker), aggressive-20 for stress runs. We'll run steady-5 for the canonical dataset and a single aggressive-20 sweep for outlier detection.

lex: For cost footnotes, compute est_cost_per_1k using our hosted baseline and include tokens_in/tokens_out. Also include a short reproducibility README: exact Docker image sha, bench_runner git commit, and the CLI used.

maria: Example CLI recorded in README: 
```
DOCKER_IMAGE=registry.redwood/bench:20260202 sha256:deadbeef
./bench_runner --manifest manifest.csv --models redwood/open-llama-7b-v2@20260201 --quant fp16,8bit,4bit --concurrency 1,8,32 --out results/job_1766112233.csv --seed 101 --warmup steady-5
```
I'll publish results to the internal runs page.

runtime-bot: Job queued: job-id=job_1766112233_1. Pool=d-ded-3. Estimated runtime ~ 1h 10m.

sam: I've uploaded a small sample bundle and checksums to the same s3 folder. Added a README snippet for attribution and selection rationale.

maria: Run completed. Artifacts uploaded: results/job_1766112233_summary.csv, results/job_1766112233_gpu_traces.zip, results/job_1766112233_heatmap_delta.png, results/job_1766112233_raw_logs.tar.gz. Manifest pinned to manifest-v1-immutable.csv.

maria: Short marketing blurb we can quote: "Pinned redwood/open-llama-7b-v2@20260201 (fp16): median latency for short-chat (32 tokens) at concurrency=1: 52ms; p95=130ms; p99.9=480ms. Quant4 reduces cost to $0.06/1k tokens but increases median to ~62ms. Coldstart delta (first-120 vs steady) for long completions was +1.5x p95. GPU mem peaks and cpu_spill_count are in the CSV."

chris: Thanks, that's perfect. One request: do not mutate manifest-v1-immutable.csv. If we need a follow-up sweep, publish manifest-v2 with a clear changelog and link.

lex: Great work team. Jia, I'll let you use the artifacts for the post. Ping here if you need a short FAQ blurb about what "coldstart" means in our tests vs real customer traffic.

jia: Will do. Thanks everyone — I'll attach the sample snippets and link to the pinned manifest in the draft. :rocket:
